result.title: Same Measurements, Different Velocity Risk: Complementary Rolling-Shutter Readouts under Clock Uncertainty
result.comment: 36 pages, including appendices. Lunshuo Tian and Dongheng Liu contributed equally
result.summary: Camera rigs with identical measurement budgets can have different velocity estimation rates when exposure timing is uncertain. We establish this distinction for rolling-shutter reconstruction with two calibrated moving anchors, unknown scene points, and independently unknown auxiliary poses and clocks. On the same fixed local physical class near a separated lateral rig, repeated readouts have worst-case squared velocity risk at least of order $σρ_{\mathrm{eff}}$, whereas complementary readouts have minimax risk of order $σ^2$, for a fixed admissible clock displacement $ρ_{\mathrm{eff}}>0$ as the noise standard deviation $σ$ tends to zero. A finite physical compensation path gives the lower bound; a nonlinear velocity inverse proves complementary stability. All motion, structure, pose, and clock nuisances remain unknown. We identify mounting configurations in which both designs become regular and quantify the risk floor induced by metric uncertainty. We quantify full-parameter domains with independent 6-ms clocks and test in-domain reconstruction under paired noise and a depth-offset intervention. Raster studies examine image formation and calibration sensitivity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在曝光时钟不确定、位姿与场景均未知的设定下，比较相同测量预算的 rolling-shutter 双锚点相机布局，给出重复读出与互补读出的速度估计 minimax 风险阶数差异及相应下界与稳定性证明。
AI.relevance_reason: 这属于多视图几何与估计理论的成像/标定问题，不涉及 VLM 内部表示、推理状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策；「complementary readout」与 latent 多读出仅是字面相似，未提供可核查的借鉴线索，故排除。
